methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $105M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
EarthGrid is a Seed-stage transportation company that has raised $105.3M to date. The relevant comparison universe consists of six private Transportation firms including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, and Olympian Motors; no public Transportation comps provide adequate methodological grounding for this early-stage valuation.

The Stage-Progression method is the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($105.3M) as a proxy for base value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $263M. The Peer-Median method does not apply here: while three same-sector peers exist in Transportation, the narrow filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier—identified zero datapoints meeting the minimum threshold of three comps, making sector-wide median comparison unreliable.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $224M (low) to $303M (high), with a median point of $263M. This narrow derivation reflects methodological constraint rather than analytical confidence. Key uncertainties center on the appropriateness of the 2.5x step multiplier for this particular capital profile and sector, the composition and stage distribution of the Transportation peer set, and whether raised capital accurately proxies pre-valuation in an illiquid, early-stage context. Refinement would require either expanded peer data at comparable stages or alternative cost-of-capital benchmarks.
